Data:Slnev.coquille.visiting.denzil.json.startdescription: Coquille tugs at Denzil's hair and asks him playfully when he will be shorn. He says only 'When it be needful', and moves irritably away from her. They do not speak again.

Data:Slnev.coquille.visiting.killes.json.startdescription: Coquille, it transpires, grows orchids. Mr Kille, a keen gardener, is very interested. Mrs Kille keeps a proprietary eye on them both to ensure that his interest is not unnecessarily inflamed. [Lesson: Orchids & Narcotics]

Data:Slnev.coquille.visiting.timothy.jso.startdescription: Reverend Timothy, having secured the attention of an attractive woman prepared to listen to his sermons, is now elucidating his previous and his next intended Christmas sermon. Coquille fastens her smile more charmingly on her face. Her eyes travel the room from end to end. There is no escape. [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.coquille.yvette.json.startdescription: Coquille asks Yvette what she knows of the line of Kelemdu, the 'Black Dove'. Yvette describes a Henavek folk-tale in which the Black Dove is assigned the wardenship of the Moon-marches by Henavek himself - a folk-tale associated with Brancrug. [Lesson: Sea Stories]

Data:Slnev.coquille.zachary.json.startdescription: Zachary and Coquille discuss the ways in which the Hours 'restrain and constrict' their rivalries, to prevent war in the Mansus. Zachary feels the 'restraints and constrictions' are growing weak. Coquille seems titillated by the prospect, but Zachary moves his head from side to side in negation. 'The Worms,' he whispers. [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]

Data:Slnev.corso.agdistis.json.startdescription: Agdistis and Corso are chatting amicably about growing up in the ways of the Sun. Apparently they were both choirboys. ('I know, I know,' says Corso. 'Then I started smoking.) [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.corso.aladim.json.startdescription: Corso is eager to hear more about Yarden of Nishapur, who al-Adim may have known long ago… although al-Adim grows chillier when Corso's interest crystallises into curiosity about the location of certain valuable texts. [Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]

Data:Slnev.corso.arthur.json.startdescription: Corso and Arthur have, it seems, been corresponding clumsily in half-learnt Ericapaean. Arthur has made more progress: he explains, very quietly, that he has had help from Julian Coseley. 'Is he actually alive?' Corso asks sceptically. 'Alive? What's alive?' responds Arthur. 'Is the Empire alive?' [Lesson: Ericapaean]

Data:Slnev.corso.arun.json.startdescription: Corso and Arun are chuckling together about Musgrave Dewulf's theories on the Great Ink porphyrine. [Lesson: Inks of Revelation]

Data:Slnev.corso.azita.json.startdescription: Corso and Azita are discussing recently discovered letters supposedly sent by the Abbess Melancthe to Gunnhild, daughter of Harold. Their musings on its contents are punctuated with bald estimates of their possible value. [Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]

Data:Slnev.corso.chaima.json.startdescription: 'Hateful tongue,' Corso says gloomily. 'But it's hard to stop speaking it once you start, you know, Chaima? Even when you stumble into a sticky patch.' [Lesson: Hyksos]

Data:Slnev.corso.connie.json.startdescription: Last time, Connie evinced suspicion that Corso might have been connected with the theft of the Bureau's copy of the Calicite Supplications. It seems it subsequently turned up after a cataloguing error was resolved. It is rare to see Connie so off-balance. Corso is celebrating with a relentless lecture on Sisterhood heresies. [Lesson: Tridesma Hiera]

Data:Slnev.corso.coquille.json.startdescription: Corso is trying to impress Coquille with an impromptu recitation of the Thirsting Tantra. His pronunciation is eccentric, but Coquille seems unexpectedly interested. Eventually, it becomes apparent even to Corso that she's just angling for the location of a copy, but Corso seems unabashed. [Lesson: Orchids & Narcotics]

Data:Slnev.corso.dagmar.json.startdescription: Corso and Dagmar are enjoying an entirely theoretical discussion of how locks might be subverted through vulgar nyctodromy. And whether Teresa Galmier was a nyctodromist (Dagmar) or a horomachist (Corso). [Lesson: Lockworks & Clockworks]

Data:Slnev.corso.douglas.json.startdescription: Douglas and Corso chat affably about church. (Douglas used to be a chapel-goer, but Mrs Moore disapproves.) [Lesson: Sacra Solis Invicti]

Data:Slnev.corso.ehsan.json.startdescription: Corso insists to Ehsan that Teresa Galmier visited his bookshop in Oxford, in person. 'She used a different name. So I didn't want to embarrass her. She's changed. But it's her. But she's changed. Taller. Well, something like taller, not taller exactly. Stop laughing, Ehsan - ' [Lesson: Purifications & Exaltations]

Data:Slnev.corso.fraser.json.startdescription: Fraser and Corso debate Medusa's Riddle: 'What Is Not Seen?' Corso gestures nonchalantly with his cigarette: 'If if's not seen, the Hours don't know where it happened. In the end, 'it's all about provenance.' [Lesson: Pentiments & Precursors]

Data:Slnev.corso.hokobald.json.startdescription: Corso adroitly flatters Hokobald into an impromptu lesson in the sigillography of Deep Mandaic. [Lesson: Deep Mandaic]

Data:Slnev.corso.morgen.json.startdescription: Corso banters with Morgen about the actual composition of her fabled 'key of black sapphire', which she insists is metaphorically glass, and which he suggests is a stained glass window 'somewhere quiet'… [Lesson: Glaziery & Lightsmithing]

Data:Slnev.corso.olympe.json.startdescription: Corso chaffs Olympe about her recent review of a performance of Menander's 'The Burning Woman', which she considers an outright manifesto for the creation of new Hours - 'Gods-from-Steel'. She acknowledges that it's an absurd idea… but disagrees that the director thought it was absurd. [Lesson: Transformations & Liberations]

Data:Slnev.corso.serena.json.startdescription: Serena and Corso gloomily dispute the poet Kalle's menacing aphorism: 'A star is a pin-prick, but the Sun is a wound.' Corso believes it presages the later division of the Sun; Serena suggests it anticipates a horrific ending to the Vagabond's prophesied pilgrimage up to the Glory... [Lesson: Pyroglyphics]

Data:Slnev.corso.stanislav.json.startdescription: Corso and Stanislav speak of the dreams that follow the consumption of the dark liquor called 'leathy', and their conversations with the Moth-name Knotwingnot. Both of them agree, almost convincingly, that they have always ignored its advice. [Lesson: Orchids & Narcotics]

Data:Slnev.corso.visiting.denzil.json.startdescription: Denzil teaches Corso a few words of Kernewek Henavek, the ancient tongue still used in some of Brancrug Village's winter ceremonies. He refers to it as 'Tavas Mytern' - perhaps 'the King Tongue' - and speaks not of 'it' but of 'him', as if the language were a living king indeed. [Lesson: Henavek]

Data:Slnev.corso.visiting.killes.json.startdescription: Corso has brought a volume of Franklin Bancroft's poetry for Mr Kille to read - he claims to see parallels with Kille's own work. Kille is grateful, but clearly cautious. He agrees at last to borrow it overnight on the promise that it is not a gift, and Corso will drop by to reclaim it before he leaves. (Mr Kille indicates that in Brancrug, they are wary of accepting gifts from visitors to the House.) [Lesson: Applebright Euphonies]

Data:Slnev.corso.visiting.timothy.json.startdescription: Timothy is relentlessly regaling Corso with his favourite moorland walks. [Lesson: Stone Stories]

Data:Slnev.corso.yvette.json.startdescription: Yvette and Corso discuss the reckoner mobs - the predatory merchants of years-of-life. Yvette tentatively suggests that she might like Corso to put her in touch with the reckoners, if he can… but he discourages her. 'Do you know what sanding is? Or dolling? Find out, Dr Southey, and then ask me again.' [Lesson: Snow Stories]

Data:Slnev.corso.zachary.json.startdescription: Zachary asks Corso to teach him a prayer in Hyksos - 'in case I should die when I wake.' [Lesson: Hyksos]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.agdistis.json.startdescription: Dagmar rambles merrily at a sceptical Agdistis about the possibilities - nyctodromic and musical - of the new Hammond organs. 'Having one shipped over, put up in my organ loft,' she says happily. 'Course we'll need electricity in the organ loft first. And the castle. And put the roof back on the castle. Any chance you're rich, Aggers? Help a gel out?' [Lesson: Lockworks & Clockworks]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.aladim.json.startdescription: Dagmar and al-Adim chat happily about Medina's 'Queens of the Rivers.' [Lesson: Path & Pilgrim]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.arthur.json.startdescription: Dagmar and Arthur discuss 'transinhabitation' - the means by which Lantern-long and similar Mansus entities may manifest in mirrors and lights. (Dagmar deprecates the term 'scrining', which she considers 'cheap'.) [Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.arun.json.startdescription: Arun and Dagmar greet each other with delight and are soon engaged in another round of their perennial riddle-game; but Arun becomes haughty when he realises that Dagmar has asked him about 'Sorrow's Solvent' just to see if she can make the ex-Hooded Prince's 'teeth stick out hissing.' [Lesson: Solutions & Separations]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.azita.json.startdescription: Dagmar and Azita are discussing means to contain the wild wood-things called Hügelkinder, who apparently have been causing trouble for a business of Azita's that apparently needs quantities of guns moved through wild European regions by dead of night. [Lesson: Glassblowing & Vesselcrafting]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.chaima.json.startdescription: Dagmar is planning a visit to the Mozabite Pentapolis in Algeria 'to catch up with a wretched troublemaker.' She earnestly solicits advice on the region from Chaima (who she keeps addressing unselfconsciously as 'Charlie'). [Lesson: Sand Stories]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.connie.json.startdescription: Dagmar has decided to lecture Connie on overreach by the Suppression Bureau and its European cousins-of-the-duties, citing arguments and precedents from theology and natural philosophy. Connie is mostly listening, mostly patiently. [Lesson: Edicts Liminal]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.coquille.json.startdescription: Dagmar and Coquille are talking again about the Great Signs and the Great Scars; again their conversation is punctuated by discussion of the 'very nice Margrave' to whom Dagmar did, in fact, introduce Coquille - a fact Dagmar seems now to be regretting. [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.corso.json.startdescription: Dagmar and Corso are arguing good-naturedly about whether Abbot Geffrey's dialogues on Forculus, Limentinus and Cardea qualify as 'proper nyctodromy.'  [Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.douglas.json.startdescription: Dagmar is hectoring Douglas on Suppression Bureau overreach, but he just sits quietly smiling with his arms folded and every so often names another incident sinister enough to need Bureau intervention: 'Rheims', or 'Revek' or 'Treowen' or 'the Wildwood Club'. Each of these puts Dagmar on the back foot, but she rallies and explains why each in turn is different; this at least gives Douglas time to sip his drink or pack his pipe. [Lesson: Edicts Inviolable]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.ehsan.json.startdescription: Dagmar's warning Ehsan darkly about 'goings-on' in Vienna: 'That bloody little man. The roofs are stiff with striges, you know. They like war even more than gossip.' [Lesson: Sky Stories]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.fraser.json.startdescription: Fraser wants Dagmar's help again, this time to open a nine-locked box he has received from the Evening Isles, which he hopes might contain 'a certain map'. He flatly refuses, however, to show the box to Dagmar, who expresses indignation that he won't trust her; and the conversation founders. [Lesson: Lockworks & Clockworks]

Data:Slnev.dagmar.hokobald.json.startdescription: Hokobald and Dagmar discuss the work of Willem Harries, with particular reference to lintels and thresholds. Hokobald's habitual air of contempt thins - he listens with real interest to Dagmar's answers - but Dagmar retains a careful distance, and, after he arranges her plate and tea-spoon to illustrate her point, she eyes them sidelong and does not touch them again. [Lesson: Door & Wall]
